The Kano State Centre for Disease Control (KNCDC) said the 12 clinically confirmed cases remained the only infections identified among 313 suspected cases screened so far .
The outbreak was reported on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, prompting the deployment of health officials to the all-girls science and technical boarding school managed by the Kano State Science and Technical Schools Board.
A visit to the school on Thursday showed that normal academic activities had resumed, with teaching and learning continuing without disruption. Speaking on the latest development to LEADERSHIP Weekend, the director-general of KNCDC, Prof Muhammad Adamu, said all the affected students were responding to treatment.
He said two students with more severe symptoms were receiving intensive medical care at the isolation centre of the Infectious Diseases Hospital, Kano, while the remaining 10 with mild conditions were being treated at a temporary isolation centre established within the school. Adamu added that no death had been recorded in connection with the outbreak.
On preventive measures, the KNCDC boss said reactive vaccination was ongoing, with more than 760 students already administered the tetanus-diphtheria (TD) vaccine, while over 700 had received chemoprophylaxis to prevent further infections.
He said the exercise would continue until all students in the school were reached.
According to him, the agency has also strengthened infection prevention and control measures, including the provision of face masks, installation of handwashing facilities at strategic locations and daily monitoring by a team of health officials.
He added that a dedicated ambulance had been stationed at the Infectious Diseases Hospital to ensure prompt referral and emergency response for students requiring medical attention.
Adamu said the state was receiving support from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, the National Primary Health Care Development Agency and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to sustain the response.
He explained that medical supplies, including diphtheria antitoxin and intravenous azithromycin, were being provided regularly, while the state government was supplying other medications and infection prevention materials.
